scope: All 113 unique maintained official URLs referenced by Platform, premium-product, Forwarder and SOAR data, plus bounded current release, upgrade, compatibility, receiver, runtime, security and SOAR claims.

sourceInventory.method: Each maintained URL was fetched directly on 2026-10-05. Current product hubs, release-note indexes, Splunkbase listings, the advisory index and official GitHub Releases endpoints were also checked for newer identifiers. Successful retrieval was not treated as claim verification.
sourceInventory.outcome: 111 URLs returned successful responses. The same two historical docs.splunk.com pages remained unavailable with HTTP 403; their historical records were preserved without a new verification date.

claimChecks.section: Welcome to Splunk Enterprise 10.6; release date and planning links
claimChecks.qualification: The September 30 release record does not by itself establish an upgrade edge, support deadline, exact maintenance target, OS package, premium-app pairing or Cloud availability.
claimChecks.followUp: Continue discovery beyond 10.6 and preserve the four-segment version-format warning.

claimChecks.qualification: The table establishes release-line paths only. Exact maintenance, OS, app, receiver, topology and authorization scope remain separate.
claimChecks.followUp: Retain 9.4.x to 10.0.x or 10.2.x as the first step and monitor the versioned table for correction.

claimChecks.section: Key points for upgrading to version 10.6; direct Universal Forwarder upgrade
claimChecks.qualification: UF upgrade certification remains separate from Heavy Forwarder, receiver, topology and package evidence.
claimChecks.followUp: Keep UF-specific citations even where the displayed release-line path matches Enterprise.

claimChecks.qualification: The current matrix has no 10.6 forwarder row. Upgrade support and release certification do not establish an exact receiver pairing.
claimChecks.followUp: Keep 10.6 Enterprise receiver selections Not established until an explicit row is published.

claimChecks.section: Current Splunk Cloud Platform and Premium App versions; Supported forwarder versions

claimChecks.qualification: The page still lists Cloud 10.5, ES 8.6 and ITSI 5.0, and its forwarder table stops at 10.4.x. The 10.6 documentation path does not prove rollout, a 10.6 receiver pairing, entitlement, region or authorization.
claimChecks.followUp: Keep Cloud 10.6 as a planning milestone and 10.6 direct-receiver compatibility Not established.

claimChecks.qualification: Customer-managed Enterprise compatibility does not establish Cloud-managed availability, entitlement, authorization or exact maintenance-patch readiness.
claimChecks.followUp: Retain exact patch and KV Store prerequisites as separate implementation checks.

claimChecks.qualification: September 23 remains the newest dated service milestone. SaaS milestones are not Collector, chart, instrumentation or private-runner installation paths.

sourceRetrieval.detail: All 113 maintained official URLs were fetched: 111 returned HTTP 200 and the same two retired Enterprise 8.1/8.2 pages returned HTTP 403. The historical records were preserved without a new claim-verification date.

boundedClaimReview.detail: The current Enterprise, Cloud, Forwarder receiver/topology, premium-product, migration, Observability component, SOAR and advisory claims recorded above were separately verified.

metadataGates.detail: sync-release-metadata.cjs --check, sync-source-register.cjs --check and sync-content-revision.cjs --check passed; the generated source register contains 143 records.

tests.detail: node --test tests/*.test.cjs passed 79 of 79 tests after replacing one stale hard-coded publication-date assertion with a regression that derives the newest dated release note.

browserJourneys.detail: Pre-publication live checks confirmed the exact Enterprise 9.4 to 10.6 route, existing browser-scoped WebMCP tools and the ES canonical, legacy-alias, Cisco-theme and invalid-input routes. Post-deployment checks are reported separately.

keyboard.detail: The ES keyboard skip link preserved theme state and moved to the comparison target. Keyboard activation opened a source-context dialog and pointer activation closed it.

narrowScreen.detail: The cloud-browser surface did not expose viewport resizing; structural responsive tests are not treated as rendered narrow-screen proof.

pdfExport.detail: No native print-to-PDF artifact or page-by-page pagination surface was available. Structural print tests remain separate.

downloadedHtml.detail: The dated snapshot action did not expose a browser download event within ten seconds, so no downloaded file or independent reopen was claimed.

screenPdfHtmlWebMcpAgreement.detail: Live screen and read-only browser-scoped WebMCP were available for the representative Enterprise route. PDF and independently reopened HTML agreement were not performed.

liveDeployment.detail: Publication and post-deployment verification occur after this audit artifact is finalized and are reported separately; this field is not pre-marked passed.
